lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: Imaginative Poems: The Magic Box
lesson.summary: Read imaginative poems, then write and perform your own magic box lines.
learning_objectives: Write and perform two lines of your own

standards.text: Listen to, discuss and recite poems; read with intonation; discuss word meaning and imagery; write poetry

success_criteria: I can read a poem with expression
I can find imagery in a poem
I can write and perform two lines
lesson.real_life: Lanterns at Eid, rain on a Lahore roof, snow in Gilgit, and British nursery rhymes with Urdu rhymes said aloud.

warm_up.prompt: Rhyming words end with the same sound.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what can a poet put in a magic box?
blocks.say: Today we open a magic box. What will we find inside?

blocks.alt: A small old wooden box with metal clasps sitting on dark blue cloth
blocks.caption: A wooden box with a clasp. What could be inside?
blocks.credit: Photo by OWN FILTERS on Unsplash
blocks.say: This wooden box is closed. Imagine it holds something amazing.

blocks.text: Stop 1: What is in the box?

blocks.markdown: A **poet** writes poems. A **poem** is words with shape and feeling.
blocks.say: The Magic Box is a poem by Kit Wright. The poet imagines a very special box.
The box can hold wonderful things. Some are real and some are imagined.

scenes.caption: A sound.
scenes.say: A poet can put a sound in the box. Imagine the sound of a bell.

scenes.caption: A feeling.
scenes.say: A poet can put a colour or a feeling. Imagine the colour of joy.

scenes.caption: Imagination.
scenes.say: A poet can put things nobody has seen. That is imagination.

blocks.markdown: A **verse** is a group of lines in a poem.
blocks.say: A poem is made of lines. A group of lines is a verse.
A poet uses imagery. Imagery means words that make a picture in your mind.

scenes.caption: A verse.
scenes.say: Here are two lines. They make a small verse.

scenes.caption: Imagery.
scenes.say: A pocket of stars is imagery. We can see it in our mind.

scenes.caption: See, hear, feel.
scenes.say: The best poems make us see, hear and feel.

question.prompt: Imagery means words that make a picture in your mind.
question.hint: Think of stars in a pocket.
question.explanation: Imagery paints a picture with words.

blocks.title: Zainab's magic box
blocks.transcript: Zainab finds a magic box. She opens it slowly. Out comes a sunrise over Badshahi Mosque. Then the smell of rain on a Lahore roof. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter, the rain sings. Next, snow in Gilgit, soft as a cloud. A glowing lantern lights up the room. The last thing is Nani's laughter. It warms the whole box. Zainab writes two lines and performs them with expression.
blocks.caption: Zainab opens an imaginary box and pulls out wonderful things.

points: A verse is a group of lines
blocks.say: Let us remember. A poet imagines things. A verse has lines. Imagery makes pictures.

scenes.say: Read slowly when the poem feels calm. Read faster when it feels excited.

blocks.goal: Move each line. Things you can really find go in Real. Wonderful made-up things go in Imagined.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Pick things for your box

blocks.markdown: Pick items for your own magic box.
blocks.say: Now write your own magic box lines. Choose wonderful things.

blocks.markdown: Use places and smells you know.
blocks.say: A sunrise over Badshahi Mosque could go in a box. So could the smell of rain on a Lahore roof.

blocks.markdown: Eid lanterns glow in many homes.
blocks.say: Snow in Gilgit or a lantern at Eid could go in too.

blocks.markdown: Any special thing can go in your box.
blocks.say: In the UK, you might pick a frosty morning or a church bell.

blocks.markdown: Write two lines, then perform them.
blocks.say: Write two lines. Make them as imaginative as you can.

scenes.caption: Line one.

scenes.caption: Line two.
scenes.say: Write a second line. Add one more special thing.

scenes.caption: Perform.
scenes.say: Perform your poem with a lively voice. Friends listen and clap.
